text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Karachi continued to face wheat-flour shortages during Eid al-Adha holidays, but the Sindh provincial food department said the situation would improve in the next 48 hours.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has hinted that the flour crisis could have been caused to please a neighbouring country and demanded a judicial inquiry.
- The Saudi authorities have listed 31 Pakistanis killed in a fire and stampede at Mina during the haj pilgrimage.
- Five people, including two brothers, drowned in the sea while picnicking off Gaddani beach near Karachi on Saturday.
- Preliminary estimates of the recently-explored natural gas well in Kirthar range suggest it could be the second biggest gas reserve in Pakistan after Sui.

- The government has formally received a go-ahead from the World Bank and the IMF to implement its revival of economic reforms package with special emphasis to cut the budget deficit to 4.0 percent during the next financial year.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan is expected to provide a credit line of 35 billion rupees for small and medium exporters under the Export Re-finance Scheme to the banks.
- A four-member Pakistan delegation led by Federal Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz reached Paris to attend the Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium meeting opening on April 22.
- India's prime minister-designate I.K. Gujral said his government would continue to try to improve relations with all neighbouring countries including Pakistan.
- Despite low economic activity, deposits of banks listed at the Karachi Stock Exchange swelled by 24.9 percent in 1996.

- The government has arrested former Punjab provincial food minister Iqbal Tikka for ordering the release of huge quantities of wheat from government warehouses during his tenure, thus creating flour shortages in the province.
- The government plans to lay off 200,000 public sector employees in the next few months to reduce its non-developmental expenses.
- Pakistan Air Force chief Air Marshal Abbas Khattak may seek early retirement after the recent scandal involving PAF officers' involvement in drug trafficking.
